classes.name: Proton pump inhibitors
classes.description: Proton pump inhibitors: omeprazole (Prilosec), pantoprazole (Protonix), esomeprazole (Nexium), lansoprazole (Prevacid, SoluTab), rabeprazole (Aciphex), dexlansoprazole (Dexilant), omeprazole/sodium bicarbonate (Zegerid, Konvomep). Capsules, tablets, packets and suspensions. Not H2 blockers or vonoprazan.
classes.plainDescription: A once-a-day pill that shuts down most stomach acid. Used for reflux, ulcers and to protect the stomach.
classes.indication: GERD, erosive esophagitis, ulcers, H. pylori

classes.name: Potassium-competitive acid blocker
classes.description: Vonoprazan (Voquezna tablets; Voquezna Triple Pak and Dual Pak for H. pylori). Brand only, no generic. Usually a step after PPIs. If the plan lists no vonoprazan, that is the finding: pick Voquezna as the reference product and record the barrier.
classes.plainDescription: A newer brand-name acid blocker, used when the usual acid pills haven't worked.
classes.indication: Erosive esophagitis, heartburn from GERD, H. pylori

classes.name: H2 blockers
classes.description: Histamine-2 receptor antagonists: famotidine (Pepcid; tablets, suspension), cimetidine, nizatidine. Prescription strengths. Not PPIs.
classes.plainDescription: A milder acid pill, often taken at bedtime or as needed.

records.verificationNote: PPI rows on PDF p.62 (printed p.46), section ULCER DRUGS. Pick omeprazole DR 20 mg capsule, Tier 3, no PA, no QL on that strength. Dexilant and Konvomep are not listed; recorded nonformulary under the closed-formulary statement (PDF p.2, p.5). Judgment: the guide also says 'All generic medications are covered unless specifically excluded' (PDF p.3); read with the closed-formulary wording, which is the specific rule for unlisted drugs. Zegerid and Prilosec brands are not listed either; generic omeprazole is covered, so not recorded as separate barriers. [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Brand-only nonformulary rules rest on the guide's own wording: "Brand name medications not listed in the medication list are not covered" (PDF p.2) and "Brand Name medications are covered only if they are included in the Closed Formulary list" (PDF p.3); exception route: Coverage Exception Process, PDF p.12 (printed XI). The p.5 line "any medications not on the formulary ... are not covered" is overridden for generics by "All generic medications are covered unless specifically excluded by your plan" (PDF p.3), so no generic is recorded as nonformulary from absence. Cover and p.2-3 headers say November 2026; reference relabeled, id unchanged.]

[Sonnet check 2026-11-06: Pick changed from the suspension to the 20 mg tablet, the form prescribers write for adults. Row "famotidine oral tablet 20 mg, 40 mg" is Tier cell E (p. 34); the suspension and cimetidine are Tier 1. The PDL gives no reason for the E code. Separately, p. 5 says benefit designs "allow us to exclude a medication if determined to be Therapeutically Equivalent to another covered product or OTC option", and famotidine 20 mg is sold OTC, but this is an inference and does not explain the 40 mg strength. A human should confirm tablet coverage.] [Reused: same national UHC PDL]
